text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended higher reflecting technical gains in New York, where March raws broke through their previous high and touched off fund buy stops. Forecasts by the Indian Sugar Mills Association that output in 1996/97 could fall by 15 per cent should not have any impact on prices as this was generally expected and will have no consequences for the country's trading position due to excessive stocks. March ended $3.50 higher at $303.50 per tonne, while May added $2.90 to close at $301.30 per tonne. In New York raw sugar futures settled higher on fund short covering. ASIA - A 10 percent VAT slapped on all sugar imports from CIS countries as well as low prices on the Russian market due to oversupply has resulted in sharply lower sugar imports in the third quarter of 1996. Total sugar imports in October/December 1996 amounted to 304,126 tonnes, raw value, sharply down from 857,527 tonnes imported in the like period the previous year. Despite this drop total imports in calendar year 1996 were up at 3.236 million tonnes against 3.186 million tonnes in 1995 and 2.894 million tonnes in 1994. BRAZIL - Sugar production up to January 16 amounted to 13.673 million tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 12.875 million tonnes, official figures show. Total production in the Center South amounted to 11.310 million tonnes compared to 10.176 million tonnes, while output in the north-northeast reached 2.362 million tonnes, down from 2.698 million tonnes in the like period the previous year. Alcohol production up to January 16 was 13.720 billion litres compared to 12.182 billion litres in 1995/96. INDIA - The director general of the Indian Sugar Mills Association (ISMA), S.L. Jain, told Reuters that sugar production in 1996/97 (October/September) is expected to reach around 14 million tonnes, white value, compared with 16.5 million tonnes last year. The fall in production was ascribed to a drop in yields by about 15 to 17 per cent. However, Jain said this is not a worrisome development because initial stocks were around 8 million tonnes, 5 million tonnes above normal carry over stocks of 3 million tonnes. Jain expects the country still to have some surplus stocks, not withstanding the likely drop in production this year.

The European Union awarded 22,750 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 45.519 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on Wednesday. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to February 5 reached 1,419,350 tonnes, which compares to 1,588,148 tonnes last year. Iran's Government Trading Corporation (GTC) has tendered to buy 14,000 tonnes of white sugar for April delivery at a price of $303 a tonne, trade sources said. The sugar will most likely come from the EU, Thailand and Brazil.
